feature: The Story page — the judge screen (`/story/[id]`), and the home of the discussion layer
summary: The Story page is the one surface where a user settles two questions — "is this real?" and "am I early or late?" — and then takes exactly one action determined by the CONFIRMED coin count. Evidence (source posts, virality grid, momentum curve, lifecycle verdict, lead-time proof) occupies the left column; the coin section sits directly under it as the single action; discussion occupies a sticky right column, because other people's takes are part of the judgement and the stamp on each comment is the earliness thesis applied to people. It must be a routed PAGE, not a modal: a story needs a shareable URL, the lead-time claim is unfalsifiable without a linkable proof surface, and the discussion column is a priority feature that a 520px sheet with a 460px-max-height feed structurally cannot carry.
mechanism:
## 0. PAGE vs MODAL — the recommendation, with reasoning

**Ship it as a route: `apps/web/src/app/(app)/story/[id]/page.tsx`. Delete `renderNarrativeModal()` (site/index.html:2186–2241). There is no modal variant.**

Six reasons, in order of force:

1. **The lead-time claim is unfalsifiable without a URL.** The whole product asserts "we saw this 31 minutes before crypto did." That claim is only credible if a third party can open the exact page, see the two permalinks (source post + first crypto post) and the promoted_at timestamp, and check it. `docs/product/insidor-flow.html` already lists "a shared link" as an entry to the Story page. The current router (`docs/research/design-interaction-model.md` §1.1) has no URL, no hash, no pushState — every modal is unlinkable by construction.
2. **The discussion column cannot fit.** The prior study's own CSS caps the feed at `max-height:460px` inside a `max-width:520px` sheet with `max-height:min(640px, 100dvh - 32px)`. At the specified comment height (22px avatar row + 2-line body + stamp line + acts row ≈ 104px) that is **four comments visible**, with the composer, the moderation warning, and the pre-stamp competing for the same 640px. Discussion is a priority feature; 4 visible comments is a preview, not a discussion.
3. **The modal root actively destroys the page.** `ensureModalRoot()` + `root.innerHTML=…` means opening the Create-Coin sheet from inside the story modal **destroys the story modal** (interaction model §1.5). The story page's primary action in two of four coin states is Create. The architecture is incompatible with the feature.
4. **Realtime fights `body{overflow:hidden}`.** Comments arrive over Supabase Realtime. Inserting into a scroll-locked overlay with a nested `overflow-y:auto` produces scroll-chaining and jump-to-top on every arrival on iOS. A page owns the document scroll and can use a `3 new ↑` pill without fighting the browser.
5. **Nine entry points converge here** (flow doc: card body, See the N coins, coin-page band, Search row, Following row, Sold row, Live rail, shared link, claim page). A surface with nine entrances and a shareable outbound link is a page.
6. **Evidence density.** Source posts + 7-cell stat grid + momentum chart + lifecycle line + 4-mark timeline + coin section + outcome band + cluster posts table is ~1,400px of vertical content. In a 472px sheet that is a scroll tube; in a 1fr column at 1440px it is one screen plus one scroll.

**What we keep from the modal:** the two-column split (evidence left, people right) — that idea is right and survives verbatim. **What changes:** it becomes a page-level grid instead of a sheet-level one, the right column becomes sticky and full-height, and the right rail (`aside.rail`) is hidden on this route (the discussion column takes its slot), reachable again via the existing `.rail-reopen` control from component-inventory §6.9.

**URL contract:**
```
/story/[id]                       canonical
/story/[id]?sort=newest           discussion sort (default: earliest, omitted from URL)
/story/[id]?coins=open            n>=2 arrives with the coin table expanded + 2s highlight
/story/[id]#c-<comment_id>        comment permalink; scrolls + 2s cyan flash on that .cm
/story/[id]#coins                 anchor target of the "See the N coins" primary
```
`generateMetadata()` emits og:title = story title, og:description = "We saw this 31 minutes before crypto did. 2.4M views, 1 coin." og:image = top post media. The shared link is the growth loop; it must render correctly in a DM preview.

## 1. THE COIN-STATE SELECTOR — D1 in one pure function

`features/narratives/model/coin-state.ts` — pure, no React, no I/O, unit-tested. This is the single place the ONE RULE is implemented.

```ts
export function coinState(matches: CoinMatch[], tier: CoinabilityTier) {
  const confirmed = matches
    .filter(m => m.verdict === 'CONFIRMED' && m.mint_time != null)   // G1: null mint_time can never be CONFIRMED
    .sort(byMcapDesc_thenMintTimeAsc);
  const unsure = matches.filter(m => m.verdict === 'UNSURE');        // never enters the switch — this is D1

  if (tier === 'never')    return { render: false };                 // D3: page does not exist
  if (tier === 'no_create' && confirmed.length === 0)
    return { primary: null, confirmed, unsure, notice: 'no_create' };// discussable, not mintable

  switch (confirmed.length) {
    case 0:  return { primary: { label: 'Create coin',  href: `/create?story=${id}` }, confirmed, unsure };
    case 1:  return { primary: { label: `Buy $${confirmed[0].ticker}`, href: `/coin/${confirmed[0].mint}` }, confirmed, unsure };
    default: return { primary: { label: `See the ${confirmed.length} coins`, anchor: '#coins' }, confirmed, unsure };
  }
}
```

`unsure.length` appears in the return value and **nowhere in the branch condition**. The ambiguous "buy which one?" state is not suppressed by copy — it is not expressible.

**Buying never happens on this page.** All three primaries are navigations or anchors. Per the flow doc's own fix: "Stories never buy. Coins buy." `Buy $HORN` routes to `/coin/<mint>` scrolled to the trade box.

**Conflict flagged:** `docs/research/03-system-design.md` §5.9 specifies CONFIRMED n≥2 → primary `Buy $TICKER` (highest score) with a secondary "3 more coins". The founder's ONE RULE says n≥2 → "See the N coins". **I have implemented the ONE RULE and consider §5.9 superseded** — a default Buy at n≥2 is exactly the ambiguous state the rule exists to delete. Needs a one-line confirmation.

**Ranking inside the confirmed list:** `mcap DESC, then mint_time ASC, then liquidity DESC`. The flow doc's rule is sayable out loud — "the biggest is the one with the most money in it" — and printed under the table. §5.9's score-first ranking is not sayable and is not shown to users. Row 1 gets `BIGGEST` only when `mcap[0] >= 2 × mcap[1]`; otherwise **no row is badged** and the table header reads "No coin is clearly biggest — the top two are within 2×." Earliest mint gets a separate `FIRST` badge, always.

## 2. LEAD TIME — the formula, and rendering it honestly when negative

```
t_crypto  = min(t_mint, t_ct)                        -- either may be null
lead_min  = (t_crypto - promoted_at) / 60000

promoted_at   set ONCE at PROMOTE, never updated, never recomputed
t_mint        first Solana mint matched to this story (PumpPortal stream)
t_ct          first of ~300 polled crypto-Twitter accounts to mention the entity (2 min poll)
```

Render table — the verdict-bar cell and the timeline agree in every case:

| condition | verdict cell | colour | timeline | sentence |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `lead_min > 0` | `+31m` | `--lime` | promote mark left of crypto mark | "We promoted this 31 minutes before the first crypto mention." |
| `lead_min < 0` | `−12m` (U+2212 minus, tabular) | `--red` | **crypto mark left of promote mark, connector red** | "Crypto got here first. The first crypto mention was 12 minutes before we promoted this." |
| `lead_min == 0` | `0m` | `--muted` | marks stacked | "Dead heat — same minute." |
| `t_crypto == null` | `+2h14m` + `and counting` sub | `--ion` | promote mark, open-ended arrow right | "No crypto account has mentioned this yet. 2h14m and counting." |
| `promoted_at == null` | `not promoted` | `--dim` | timeline hidden | "This story has not been promoted. Nothing is being claimed." |
| `earliness_eligible == false` | `already hot` | `--dim`, dashed border | timeline shown, greyed | "We first saw this post already large. It is excluded from our lead-time record." |
| mint-stream gap overlaps `[promoted_at, t_crypto]` | `unmeasurable` | `--amber` | connector amber, dashed | "The mint stream dropped from 14:31 to 14:52. We will not claim a number we could not verify." |

**No hedging vocabulary anywhere in the negative case.** Not "narrowly behind", not "slightly late". `−12m` in red, "Crypto got here first."

**Provenance line, always rendered, 9.5px `--dim` mono, under the timeline:**
`measured against 41,208 mints streamed + 300 crypto accounts polled every 2 min · t_crypto = first of either`

## 3. LIFECYCLE VERDICT LINE

State machine already specified in 03-system-design §2.5 (with hysteresis). The page renders the state as a sentence with the raw numbers behind it:

```
HEATING   "Momentum established"   R̂ >= 1.15 OR (g >= +0.020 AND v >= 0.5 reshares/min)
PEAKING   "At peak"                otherwise
COOLING   "Window narrowing"       v < 0.60·v_peak AND g <= -0.010, 2 consecutive snaps
DEAD      "Over"                   v < 0.05·v_peak OR (v < 0.2 AND tau > 90)
```

Copy pattern — headline (12.5px `--ink` 500) then evidence (12px `--muted`):
- HEATING: **"Momentum established"** / "Reshare rate 1.4× this author's own baseline and still climbing. 22 posts in the last 5 minutes, across 2 platforms."
- PEAKING: **"At peak"** / "Reshare rate flat for 2 snapshots at 38/min. This is as loud as it gets."
- COOLING: **"Window narrowing"** / "Reshares at 48% of peak for 2 consecutive snapshots. Cooling since 14:22."
- DEAD: **"Over"** / "Under 5% of peak for the last hour. 0 new posts since 15:40."

The left 3px bar of `.st-verdict` takes the state colour: cyan HEATING, lime PEAKING, amber COOLING, dim DEAD. Reuses the `.nm-about` treatment (component-inventory §7.3.4).

## 4. THE STAMP — format and the compactness rules

```ts
stamp(c) =
  "posted when " +
  fmtCount(c.snap_views) + " views · " +
  (c.snap_coin_count === 0 ? "no coin yet"
    : c.snap_coin_count === 1 ? "1 coin" : `${c.snap_coin_count} coins`) + " · " +
  age(c.snap_age_min) + " old" +
  (c.snap_coin_count > 0 ? " · " + fmtUSD(c.snap_top_mcap) : "") +
  (isEarly(c) ? " · early" : "")

isEarly(c) = c.snap_coin_count === 0
          && c.snap_views <= 0.25 * narrative.combined_views_now
```

Renders: `posted when 340K views · no coin yet · 40m old · early`
and:     `posted when 1.1M views · 2 coins · 2h old · $412.9K`

Five rules that keep it from dominating the comment:
1. **One line, never two.** `white-space:nowrap; overflow:hidden; text-overflow:ellipsis`.
2. **Three facts when there is no coin, four when there is.** `snap_top_mcap` is omitted entirely at 0 coins — `$0` reads as a bug, not a fact.
3. **Colour floor.** Whole line `--dim` (#5A5A62), the `<b>` values lifted only to `--muted` (#8A8A93). The body above it is 13.5px `--ink` General Sans — three contrast steps up. The stamp is the same weight as the `.acts` row beneath it, so it reads as chrome.
4. **`· early` is the only decorated token** — `--ion`, no background, no border, no icon. If everything is decorated nothing is.
5. **Degradation order on narrow columns:** drop mcap → drop age → drop coin count. `posted when 340K views` alone is still the whole point.

`title` attribute carries the exact values for anyone who wants them: `written 14:41:22 · 340,102 views · 0 coins · 40 min after promote`.

**It is a historical fact and is never recomputed.** No joins at read time. The four snap columns are written once at insert and never updated — enforced by a `BEFORE UPDATE` trigger that raises if any `snap_*` column changes.

## 5. THE POSITION BADGE — resolution at write time

Read server-side inside the insert handler, against the story's **top confirmed coin** (`confirmed[0].mint`), with an 800 ms budget.

```
lamports = await balance(user.wallet_address, mint)     // api/balance.js, Helius

lamports > 0                          -> 'has'       "holds 2.1 SOL"     lime
lamports === 0 && priorHolding        -> 'sold'      "sold"              amber
lamports === 0 && !priorHolding && confirmed.length > 0 -> 'none' "no position"  dim
confirmed.length === 0                -> 'none'      "no coin to hold"   dim
read failed / timed out (lamports null) -> 'unknown' "position unknown"  dim, dashed border
```

- `priorHolding` = a `holding` row exists for `(user_id, mint)` with `closed_at IS NOT NULL`. **Without that row we cannot distinguish "sold" from "never bought", and we must not guess** — a false `sold` is a fabricated credential.
- **A failed read never renders as `no position`.** That would be a lie in the user's favour (it implies they are not talking their book when we simply do not know). `position unknown` with a dashed border is the honest render, and it is rare enough to be unremarkable.
- **`no coin to hold`** replaces `no position` on a zero-coin story. Better English and it does not imply the commenter declined to buy something that never existed.
- Amount format: `holds 2.1 SOL` — `(lamports/1e9).toFixed(1)`, floor at `holds <0.1 SOL`. With more than one confirmed coin the badge names it: `holds 2.1 SOL · $HORN`.
- **Wallet-not-connected is unreachable for authored comments** — a connected wallet is required to post (A11 rationale: cost, not identity). It occurs only on backfilled/imported rows, which render `position unknown`.
- Read once, at write time, never again. Nine hours later the badge still says what was true when the words were written, which is the only version that means anything.

## 6. MODERATION — the address gate

```ts
const B58 = /[1-9A-HJ-NP-Za-km-z]{32,44}/g;

// storyMints is already loaded on the page — it is the coin section's own data
const storyMints = new Set([
  ...coinMatches.map(m => m.mint),                    // CONFIRMED and UNSURE both
  ...narrativeTickers.map(t => t.mint_ca).filter(Boolean)
]);

const offenders = [...body.matchAll(B58)].map(m => m[0]).filter(a => !storyMints.has(a));
const blocked   = offenders.length > 0;
```

- **UNSURE mints are allowed.** They are shown on the page; forbidding discussion of what we display would be incoherent, and warning users off a candidate is exactly the conversation we want.
- **False positives are acceptable, false negatives are not.** A 32–44 char base58 run can be a tx signature or a random token. Cost of a false positive: a warning the user edits around, with their text intact. Cost of a false negative: a shill CA under a hot story. Asymmetric, so we keep the loose regex.
- **Client check is a courtesy; the server check is the enforcement.** Same function, imported from `features/narratives/model/moderation.ts`, run in `POST /api/story/[id]/comment`. Server response on violation: `422 {reason:'address_gate', matched:'7xKX…jVn0P'}`; the row is written with `status='removed'` and `flags={rule:'address_gate', matched}` so the eval set grows itself.
- **Ships in the same release as the composer.** Not the next one. Non-negotiable (A11).

Full ladder, in cost order (from `docs/reference/insidor-social.html` §03), with the UI treatment for each:

| # | rule | server action | what the author sees | what everyone else sees |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | address gate | block, no appeal | live warning before posting; if it lands anyway, `.cm.blocked` with `.blocknote` | **nothing** |
| 2 | impersonation (edit-distance ≤2 of the story's poster or a top-50 account) | `status='held'` | amber left bar + "Held for review — your handle is close to @nordkyst_ferge. Usually under an hour." | nothing until released |
| 3 | new wallet (<24h, 0 prior tx) | 1 comment per story; held if links present | dim helper under the box: "New wallet — one comment per story until you have some history." | normal comment |
| 4a | velocity, bot signature (same body under >2 stories in 10 min) | **silent drop** — 200 OK, `status='removed'` | the comment appears in their own feed and nowhere else | nothing |
| 4b | speed limit (>3 comments / 60s, human) | 429 with `retry_after` | Post button disabled, amber countdown `slow down · 24s`, text preserved | nothing |
| 5 | generic hate/violence/sexual API | `status='held'` | "Held for review." | nothing |

**Deviation from the prior study, flagged:** `insidor-social.html` renders the blocked comment publicly with a strike-through and a red note. That is illustrative, not shippable — a publicly visible blocked comment still delivers the CA impression, which is the entire payoff the spammer wanted. **Blocked and held rows are visible to their author only** (`where status='visible' or author_id = $me`). The strike-through treatment is kept exactly as designed, just scoped to one viewer.

## 7. OUTCOME CLASSIFICATION (D2) — nightly job

```
if (mint_stream_gap overlaps [promoted_at, t_crypto])       -> UNMEASURABLE
else if (confirmed_coin_count == 0)                         -> NO_COIN
else if (lead_min < 0)                                      -> LATE
else if (peak_mcap >= 250_000)                              -> HIT
else                                                        -> DUD
```
Runs when `lifecycle = DEAD` and `now - promoted_at > 24h`. `peak_mcap` = max `narrative_tickers.mcap` observed across all confirmed coins over the story's life (needs a time series — flagged below). The 250k threshold is a founder call.

The outcome band's default state everywhere it aggregates (Search → Finished) is **All**, never Hits. Per D2: if a user has to opt in to seeing misses, the record is marketing.

## 8. DISCUSSION SORT

```sql
-- Earliest (DEFAULT)
order by c.snap_views asc nulls last, c.created_at asc
-- Newest
order by c.created_at desc
```
**"Earliest" means "written when the story was smallest", not "oldest by clock".** They diverge: a comment written 3h ago at 2.4M views ranks below one written 40m ago at 340K if the story was rediscovered. That divergence is the feature — it surfaces the takes made under uncertainty. The header carries the definition on hover: *"Earliest = written when the story was smallest."*

Realtime arrivals while sorted Earliest do **not** splice into the middle. A `3 new ↑` cyan pill pins to the top of the feed; click scrolls to top and re-sorts. Under Newest, arrivals prepend with the `pop .4s` animation.

## 9. STALE-PIPELINE DETECTION

```
stale = (now - max(worker_cycle_log.ran_at)) > 10 min
paused = window._scoringPaused  (existing signal)
```
When stale: an amber band (reuse `.scoring-paused-banner` skin) pins above the verdict bar — "Pipeline last ran 34 minutes ago. Views, momentum and coin matches on this page may be stale." The REACH cell stops its `nmTickUp` animation and gains a `stale` chip. Numbers are still shown — hiding them would be worse — but they are labelled.

## DOES NOT EXIST — every one of these blocks a region of this page

**BLOCKER 1 — `coin_match`. The entire matching verdict has nowhere to live. Without it the UNSURE state is unrenderable and D1 cannot ship.**
```sql
create table coin_match (
  narrative_id  uuid not null references narratives(id),
  mint          text not null,
  verdict       text not null,             -- CONFIRMED | UNSURE | REJECTED
  relation      text not null,             -- DERIVED | ADOPTED | MENTIONED | SUGGESTED
  score         numeric,                   -- calibrated. NEVER rendered as a number.
  s_mint_in_post numeric, s_img numeric, s_text numeric, s_tick numeric, s_social numeric,
  strong_channels int,                     -- drives the categorical chip copy
  mint_time     timestamptz,               -- min(pairCreatedAt) across ALL pairs. NULL = fail closed.
  delta_min     int,                       -- mint_time - earliest_post_at, may be negative
  matched_at    timestamptz default now(),
  primary key (narrative_id, mint)
);
create index on coin_match (narrative_id, verdict);
```

## QUERY SHAPES

**Q1 — page load, evidence (RSC, one round trip)**
```sql
select n.*,
  (select json_agg(p order by p.views desc)
     from narrative_posts p where p.narrative_id = n.id and p.pruned_at is null) as posts
from narratives n where n.id = $1;
```

**Q2 — momentum series** — `select t, views, reshares, posts from narrative_series where narrative_id = $1 order by t` (≈120 rows for a 2h story; downsample to 60 client-side).

**Q3 — coin section** (drives the primary button; must be one query so the button cannot disagree with the table)
```sql
select cm.mint, cm.verdict, cm.relation, cm.strong_channels, cm.delta_min, cm.mint_time,
       cm.s_img, cm.s_text, cm.s_tick, cm.s_mint_in_post,
       t.ticker, t.name, t.mcap, t.liquidity, t.holders, t.age_min
from coin_match cm
left join narrative_tickers t on t.mint_ca = cm.mint and t.narrative_id = cm.narrative_id
where cm.narrative_id = $1 and cm.verdict in ('CONFIRMED','UNSURE')
order by (cm.verdict = 'CONFIRMED') desc, t.mcap desc nulls last, cm.mint_time asc;
```

**Q4 — discussion** (paged 50, cursor on the sort key)
```sql
select c.*, u.handle, u.wallet_address,
       exists(select 1 from comment_vote v where v.comment_id = c.id and v.user_id = $me) as voted,
       (select count(*) from comment_vote v where v.comment_id = c.id) as votes
from comment c join app_user u on u.id = c.author_id
where c.narrative_id = $1
  and (c.status = 'visible' or c.author_id = $me)
order by case when $sort = 'earliest' then c.snap_views end asc nulls last,
         case when $sort = 'earliest' then c.created_at end asc,

limit 50;
```
Indexes already specced: `(narrative_id, created_at desc)` and `(narrative_id, snap_views asc)`.

1. resolve `app_user` from the Privy session; 401 if no wallet.
2. rate ladder: 3/60s per wallet · duplicate body across >2 stories/10min · new-wallet 1-per-story.

**Q6 — realtime** — `supabase.channel('comment:'+id).on('postgres_changes', {event:'INSERT', schema:'public', table:'comment', filter:'narrative_id=eq.'+id})`. One ref-counted socket for the app (§7.2 `shared/realtime`).

Channel readout maps s_tick/s_text/s_img/s_mint_in_post to words via fixed thresholds: >=0.60 'matches', 0.30–0.60 'weak', <0.30 'does not match', null 'not checked'. The numeric score is never sent to the client.
elements.interaction:
'View anyway' navigates to `/coin/<mint>?unverified=<story_id>`, which renders a persistent red-bordered banner and requires a second explicit confirm before its Buy is enabled (see the handoff screen). The mint is copyable so a user can verify it themselves on Solscan — giving them the tool rather than the verdict.

WHY AMBER AND NOT RED OR GREY: red means blocked/dangerous and would be a claim we cannot support — we do not know that these coins are bad, we know we cannot confirm they are related. Grey means disabled/loading and reads as a broken page. Amber is 'caution' in the settled palette and it is the only honest colour for 'we abstained'.

COMBINED STATE (>=1 CONFIRMED and >=1 UNSURE): the confirmed treatment governs the header, the button and Region 1; the unverified region renders unchanged beneath it. REJECTED matches never render at all.

ONE CONFIRMED + N UNSURE → 'Buy $TICKER' with the unverified region below

MCAP/LIQ render `—`, a `.newbadge` NEW sits beside the ticker, and a sub-line reads 'No trades yet — you would be the first buyer.' Buy stays enabled. openQuestions: The ONE RULE vs `03-system-design.md` §5.9. The system design says CONFIRMED n>=2 → primary `Buy $TICKER` (highest score) with a secondary '3 more coins'. The founder's rule says n>=2 → 'See the N coins'. I implemented the founder's rule and treat §5.9 as superseded — a default Buy at n>=2 is precisely the ambiguous state the rule deletes. Confirm, and I will amend §5.9.

'See the N coins' on the Story page is slightly degenerate — the story page IS the destination of that button when it appears on a Trending card. I specced it as an anchor to `#coins` with a 2s highlight. The alternative is a real `/story/[id]/coins` compare route with sortable numeric columns, holder concentration and safety flags (the flow doc's 'Pro' treatment). Which?

Coin ranking rule. The flow doc says the main coin is 'the one with the most money in it', with no name given when the top two are within 2×. §5.9 says rank by match score, then earliest mint, then liquidity. I ranked by mcap (sayable out loud, printable under the table) and badge FIRST separately. Confirm mcap wins.

Blocked comments: I made them visible to their author only. `insidor-social.html` renders them publicly with a strike-through. Public display still delivers the CA impression the spammer paid for. Confirm author-only.
Discussion default sort is `snap_views ASC`, not `created_at ASC` — 'written when the story was smallest', not 'oldest by clock'. They diverge on rediscovered stories. Confirm that is the intent.

The DUD threshold. I classify HIT at peak_mcap >= $250K and DUD below it. That number decides what fraction of the public record reads as a win, so it should be set deliberately and never moved afterwards.

Ship the upvote button in v1 at all? The study's own argument is that votes are farmable and the stamp gives non-gameable ranking for free. I put votes last in the build order but they are still in the design.
Reply depth: I allowed one level and flatten below it. Flat-only is simpler and harder to derail. Preference?

A story with `coinability_tier = no_create` (public tragedy, ongoing disaster) keeps a fully open composer. D3 says these are discussable. Confirm the comment box stays open on a disaster story — that is where moderation load will actually land.

The `sold` position badge requires a `holding` row to distinguish it from 'never bought'. Until `holding` exists, every zero-balance commenter renders 'no position'. Accept that gap, or delay the badge until holdings ship?

Does the position badge read against the top confirmed coin only, or against every confirmed coin summed? I specced top coin only, named when there is more than one. Summing across coins is more complete but the badge stops fitting on one line.
